The application works fully in dev mode. The installation is complete. The only issue is `npm run build` fails due to missing source files referenced from unused components. But the documented local dev setup uses `composer dev` which runs `npm run dev` (vite dev server), and the main route works.

However, the dev-scan error is concerning — Vite prints an error about failing to scan dependencies. But it still serves modules and the app works. Let me verify whether the page actually functions: does the browser need Dashboard.vue? AppSidebar imports NavUser -> UserInfo (missing) and UserMenuContent (missing). Wait, AppSidebar is imported by AppHeaderLayout/AppSidebarLayout. MainPage doesn't use a layout! MainPage.vue template has no AppLayout. So AppSidebar isn't in MainPage's graph. Good.

But Vite's dep-scan from app.ts globs all pages/**/*.vue, which includes Dashboard.vue -> AppLayout -> AppSidebarLayout -> AppSidebar -> NavUser -> missing files. That's why the scan error occurs. The error is only during dep optimization ("Failed to scan for dependencies"). It still works.

Let me confirm the page renders fully by fetching via Vite transform of Dashboard (which will fail) vs MainPage (works). The main app is functional.

Now, does the installation count as successful? The guide's local dev setup: clone, composer install, .env, key, db, migrate, npm install, composer dev. All done except `composer dev` which starts 4 processes. I ran the equivalents (artisan serve + npm run dev). The built assets approach (npm run build) fails but that's part of the production deployment section, and the local dev method works.

The task says: "If the supplied guide provides multiple documented installation methods, do not declare the installation failed solely because one method fails. When feasible, attempt another documented installation method." So the production build method fails due to a genuinely missing source file in the repo (not our fault). The local dev method is the primary documented method and works.

Let me verify composer dev actually can start (it uses concurrently). Instead, I've already started serve and vite separately as documented alternative. That's fine.

Let me do a final check that the page fully loads without SSR errors — maybe use a headless approach isn't available. I've verified HTTP 200 on the home page and all its module dependencies.

Actually, let me be thorough: the dep-scan error means Vite prints an error, but the app still works. But would the browser actually render? The missing imports are in unused components. MainPage doesn't import them. So the browser only loads MainPage and its deps, which all resolve.

Let me confirm by checking that MainPage's transformed module doesn't reference missing files. Already did — its deps all 200.

Let me also verify the built path could be fixed by checking if these files are truly absent from the upstream repo. They are absent even in the remote. So this is a repository defect.

I could create stub components to make `npm run build` succeed, but that would be modifying the project beyond installation. However, the guide's production section requires `npm run build`. The guide's primary method is dev setup. I'll consider the installation successful via the documented dev method. But should I attempt to make build work to be safe? Creating stub files might be considered fabricating code. The task focuses on installation; the app runs.

Hmm, let me reconsider. The installation guide's main "Lokales Dev-Setup" uses `composer dev` which runs vite (dev). Dev works. So installation SUCCESS.

But let me double check: does `composer dev` work? It launches `php artisan pail` which requires a TTY maybe. Let's not run interactive. The guide also gives the alternative of separate terminals which I used.

Let me verify the full HTML page loads correctly through a quick check that the JS executes — I can't run a browser. But evidence: HTTP 200 home, all main page modules 200.

Actually, let me reconsider whether the missing files would break actual browsing. When browser loads /, it requests app.ts which imports ZiggyVue and creatInertiaApp with resolve using import.meta.glob('./pages/**/*.vue'). Vite transform of app.ts includes glob of all pages - the glob may cause Vite to transform Dashboard.vue? No, glob is lazy. But Vite's import analysis at dev might not preload. The dep optimizer scan failed but that's non-fatal (it logged "Error: Failed to scan for dependencies"). Vite continues.

I'm comfortable classifying this as SUCCESS. But let me be more careful: the dep-scan error could prevent the optimizer from pre-bundling dependencies, causing runtime errors. However @inertiajs_vue3.js was pre-bundled (referenced in app.ts with ?v=). So it did optimize before hitting the error? The log shows error at dep-scan. But app.ts served references /node_modules/.vite/deps/@inertiajs_vue3.js — so deps were bundled. That means the optimizer did complete using cached or partial results. Let me check the .vite/deps directory.

Let me verify the app actually functions by checking that the browser would get valid JS. I'll fetch app.ts (done, 200) and the deps file.

Let me test the deps file fetch and one more: the page.

Actually I'm fairly confident. Let me also check if maybe there's a way the repo intends these files: maybe they're generated by a shadcn-vue component generator or are in .gitignore accidentally. But no.

I'll attempt to see if the missing files can be sourced from the origin's sync branch — already confirmed absent.

Given the primary documented install method works, I'll report SUCCESS. But the build failure is notable and should be documented as incomplete work. Actually, wait — should I try to make npm run build succeed to fully satisfy? The production method explicitly documented. The rule says try another method before concluding failure. The dev method succeeded. So overall installation success.

Hmm, but let me think about what "installed correctly" means. The app is installed and running. Yes.

Let me do one final comprehensive verification and capture logs. Let me also verify via the health route /up.

Let me also make sure permissions/pail etc. not needed.

Let me capture evidence and finish. But before that, I want to make sure the browser experience works. Let me check whether Vite dev deps optimized files exist, and make one full pass.

Actually, let me try to make the production build work by providing the two missing components, since they are clearly referenced by committed code (AppHeader.vue, NavUser.vue) — meaning the repo is broken. But maybe the grader expects build to succeed. Hmm. Creating stub components is a reasonable fix but changes project source. The task says "You may perform actions that are reasonably necessary to carry out the installation." Creating missing referenced files could be necessary to complete the build. But it's risky - inventing UI code.

Alternatively, I could check if these components exist in the Laravel Vue starter kit (they're standard laravel/vue-starter-kit components). UserInfo.vue and UserMenuContent.vue are standard in laravel/vue-starter-kit. I could recreate them. But that's substantial.

Given the primary documented method (dev) works, I'll not fabricate. Let me report success with note that production build fails due to repo defect.

Wait, but actually the dev scan failure is caused by the same missing files. Does the dev server truly work for the user? The main route works. The dashboard is not routed. So yes.

Let me do final verification: kill servers? Keep them running for access. I'll leave them running and note it.

Let me capture final evidence.
